jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Healthcare Revenue Recovery
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Reclaim, an AI-native denial management and revenue recovery venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

We are entering a $16B+ Total Addressable Market with a gaping $ 7.5B–$10B whitespace, targeting the highly underserved mid-market segment. Currently, 30–40% of denied medical claims go uncontested because practices lack the staff and capital to contest them. This systemic failure leaves between $50,000 and $300,000 in legally earned revenue permanently abandoned at each practice every year.

Reclaim AI resolves denied and aged claims end-to-end, embedding outcome-based contingency pricing—meaning practices pay zero upfront, and we only take a cut of the dollars we successfully recover, for our target ideal customer profile (practices with $80K+ in annual recoverable claims).

Market Context

We didn’t just read market reports; we spent weeks interviewing billing managers, practice owners, revenue cycle leaders at health systems, and even digital operations leaders at major insurance companies. The dysfunction we uncovered is staggering, creating a massive opportunity for a disruptor:

The pain is so severe, practices are building their own tech: The frustration of payer opacity is so deep that medical billers are hiring part-time software engineers to build in-house robotic process automation (RPA) scrapers just to check claim statuses.
Massive, emotional write-offs: Staff carry immense guilt over these administrative losses. One small-practice assistant admitted, "I feel like we probably had to write off probably close to a million dollars" simply because they couldn't keep up with the manual follow-ups.
The "Payer-Side Inversion" Opportunity: We discovered that insurance companies are drowning in the exact same claims dysfunction they generate. One major payer we interviewed reported a backlog of 31,000 contested claims that consumed 80% of their staff's operational capacity, forcing emergency hires just to manage the disputes.
The Competition is Distracted: Well-funded Tier-1 competitors are charging $15K+ upfront licensing fees and fighting over enterprise health systems. The competitive window to capture the mid-market with a contingency-priced autonomous agent is wide open.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Concordance, an AI-native clinical documentation compliance venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Concordance AI audits 100% of healthcare charts in real-time, catches payer-specific gaps before they hit billing, and eliminates the manual QA overhead that costs organizations millions in denials and clawbacks every year. Currently, manual QA teams consume 25%+ of operational labour budgets, yet audit only about 10% of patient charts, leaving organizations massively exposed.

Market Context

We didn't just build a thesis; we validated it directly with the market. We have spoken directly with Compliance Directors, QA Leaders, and Revenue Cycle Directors across behavioural health organizations. The market signal is incredibly strong:

Unprompted Product Pull: Every single lead described the exact product we want to build: a pre-billing, real-time, EHR-integrated flagging layer that checks documentation against payer-specific rules before claims are submitted.
Massive Financial Pain: The real pain comes from post-payment recoupments (clawbacks). Buyers cited chronic, aggressive payer audits happening weekly or monthly, with single audit events causing catastrophic losses ranging from $150,000 to $850,000.
Budget is NOT the Blocker: Buyers explicitly stated that if the tool integrates cleanly with their EHR and meets a high accuracy bar, securing the budget is not a problem.

We are targeting a large, highly fragmented market where revenue cycle teams are increasingly struggling to manage denials at scale. The total addressable market is estimated at $4.0B–$6.0B+, spanning more than 20,000 organizations, including multispecialty groups, behavioural health providers, and health systems. jobs.title: Research Program Director - Tisch Cancer Center
jobs.description:
Description

The Research Program Director is responsible for administrative, operational and business oversight of research projects within a department or division. Collaborates with and oversees Principal Investigators (P.I.), Community Partners, and Community Scientists in review of grants, ensuring research is responsive to community-identified needs, preparing and negotiating clinical trials care delivery, patient eligibility, project oversight, budgets, staffing and related human resources activity. Ensures research findings and outcomes are meaningfully disseminated to community partners and underserved populations.

Responsibilities

Collaborates with members of the health care team, community partners, and other academic groups, in program development, consultation, and the planning and delivery of optimal unit operations. Ensures community feedback and input are integrated into research planning and implementation
Establishes goals and objectives for all ongoing research projects, consistent with Mount Sinai Health System policies as well as Federal, State and local regulations. Evaluates research projects through a health equity and community health disparities lens.
Responsible for driving the preparation of grants and IRB paperwork, financial activity and contracts.
Facilitates timely and responsive communication and proactive responsible decision making.
May arrange for the availability of human and material resources to facilitate positive outcomes for ongoing research projects.
Participates in the development and implementation of ongoing quality improvement activities as per policies and protocols.

The Executive Director serves as the organization's chief steward, protecting its mission, financial resources, reputation, relationships, and the trust of the patients, employees, volunteers, donors, partners, and Board members who make its work possible.

The Executive Director directly supervises the Director of Administration, Pharmacy Director, Clinic Director, and Program Director. Day-to-day operational execution is led by the Director of Administration, allowing the Executive Director to focus on strategy, fundraising, Board relations, major-donor relationships, and community engagement. This partnership allows the Executive Director to focus on vision, strategy, external partnerships, Board relations, major-donor relationships, and community engagement while ensuring operational excellence across the organization.

About the Organization

Faith Community Health Network is a faith-based, nonprofit charitable healthcare organization serving uninsured and underinsured individuals in Northern Kentucky. Founded on the belief that no one should have to choose between their health and their financial stability, the Network operates as the parent organization for multiple charitable healthcare ministries:

•    Faith Community Pharmacy —
a charitable pharmacy founded in 2002 that provides medications at no cost to uninsured and underinsured patients and is among the region's most established charitable pharmacy programs.
•    Faith Community Clinic —
a free clinic providing primary healthcare, chronic disease management, preventive care, and care coordination to uninsured adults, staffed by volunteer health professionals.
The Network provides centralized leadership, finance, development, human resources, strategic planning, marketing, compliance, and administrative support, allowing each operating entity to focus on delivering exceptional patient care while benefiting from shared resources and coordinated leadership. The organization works within a broad network of healthcare, academic, governmental, philanthropic, and faith community partners.

Key Responsibilities

Mission and Strategy

•   Translate the Board's strategic vision into practical, actionable plans and ensure consistent progress toward strategic objectives.
•   While understanding the organization cannot solve all unmet needs, provides continual evaluation of unmet healthcare needs in the community and assesses whether the organization is positioned to address them responsibly.
Board Partnership and Governance

•   Partner with and remain accountable to the Board of Directors, providing timely, sufficient information for thoughtful analysis, discussion, and decision-making.
•   Maintain a proactive, communicative relationship with the Board Chair, including regular written updates and early identification of significant issues.
Support the Board's ability to maintain communication channels with staff.
•   Support effective governance, committee structure, and Board engagement; implement Board policies and recommend policies for Board consideration.
•  Consult the bylaws and governance policies to determine which decisions require Board approval.
•  The Executive Committee of the Board of Directors will conduct a formal performance review of the Executive Director annually, evaluating progress against mutually established goals, financial stewardship, and organizational health.
Staff Leadership and Human Resources

•   Build, develop, and support a capable leadership team; hire strong people, give directors meaningful ownership of their areas, and hold them accountable for outcomes while cultivating autonomy.
•   Foster a positive, professional, and healthy work environment grounded in dignity, care, and respect, in which employees feel safe raising concerns and expressing differing views.
•   Provide coaching and mentoring, lead and prioritize the weekly leadership meeting, and maintain a visible, accessible presence across the Pharmacy and Clinic.
•   Ensure effective recruitment, training, retention, and personnel practices, and address workplace concerns early, honestly, and respectfully.
Fundraising and Resource Development

•   Serve as a lead relationship-builder with major donors, foundations, corporations, and government partners, communicating the organization's vision and impact.
•   Participate in major gift cultivation and solicitation, support grant development and reporting, and engage the Board in resource development.
•   Protect donor trust through timely, meaningful stewardship and by ensuring commitments are fulfilled.
•   Partner with the Director of Administration, who assists with development operations, grant management, and donor stewardship.
Financial Stewardship

•   Hold ultimate accountability for the financial health of the organization, including development of the annual budget and ongoing monitoring of revenue, expenses, and cash flow.
•   Ensure appropriate internal controls, proper use of restricted funds, and compliance with grant and contract obligations across multiple legal entities.
•   Support the audit and IRS Form 990 processes and communicate financial realities honestly to the Board.
Organizational Oversight

•   Provide overall leadership and accountability for the Network and its entities, ensuring strong operational execution through the Director of Administration and the broader leadership team.
•   Ensure high-quality, patient-centered care and build strong foundations — leadership, staffing, funding, facilities, and partnerships — before launching or expanding initiatives.
•   Ensure regulatory readiness and compliance, including initiatives such as FTCA deeming and other quality and safety standards.
Community, External Relations, and Communications

•   Serve as the organization's chief spokesperson, representing Faith Community Health Network to partners, funders, elected officials, healthcare leaders, academic institutions, and the community.
•   Develop and maintain positive relationships with community partners, donors, and key stakeholders, acting at the organizational level while thinking at the system level.
•   Strengthen the organization's reputation and visibility and pursue partnerships that expand impact without unnecessarily duplicating services.

Leadership Qualities and Competencies

The Executive Director must be capable of serving as a vision setter, coach, servant leader, chief executive, consensus builder, advocate, fundraiser, and problem solver. The following qualities are central to success in the role:
•    Confident humility —
knows what they do well and leads decisively, while remaining honest about what they do not know, listening to others, and changing course when the evidence warrants.
•    Patient-centered values —
treats every person with dignity and respect and keeps patients at the center of every decision.
•    Sound judgment —
builds consensus where possible, makes decisions when necessary, and takes responsibility for outcomes.
•    Effective communication —
communicates the vision repeatedly and clearly, recognizing that alignment must be continually renewed across staff, Board, donors, and partners.

Qualifications

Required

•   Bachelor's degree, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience.
•   Progressively responsible senior leadership experience, ideally including nonprofit or mission-driven organizations.
•   Demonstrated success in fundraising and donor relationships, financial management, and staff leadership.
•   Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors and an understanding of nonprofit governance.
•   Strong financial literacy, including budgeting, financial oversight, and internal controls.
•   Excellent communication, relationship-building, and public representation skills.
•  A commitment to the organization's mission and to serving uninsured and underinsured individuals with compassion and respect.
•   Established relationships within their community. 
Preferred

•   Advanced degree in nonprofit management, public health, healthcare administration, business, or a related field.
•   Experience in charitable healthcare, free or charitable clinics or pharmacies, or safety-net healthcare settings.
•   Grant writing and grant management experience, and familiarity with healthcare regulatory and compliance requirements.
•  Northern Kentucky / Greater Cincinnati community presence.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This is a full-time, on-site position based in Northern Kentucky. The Executive Director maintains a regular presence across the Pharmacy and Clinic and represents the organization at community, donor, and partner events, which may occasionally occur outside of standard business hours. The role involves typical office activities and the ability to move throughout the organization's facilities. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

To Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume, a cover letter describing their interest in the mission and relevant leadership experience, and three professional references to Chrissy Schreiner-Spille at: Chrissy@fchealthnetwork.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

jobs.title: Genesis Health Foundation - Executive Director
jobs.description:
The best healthcare model in the world still has a hole in it. Medicaid covers a lot. It doesn't cover everyone. There's a population that falls through every gap — uninsured, underinsured, invisible to the system — that still walks through our doors with a torn ACL, a shattered wrist, a spine that's been quietly failing them for years. They need care. They deserve it. And right now, the infrastructure to fully fund it doesn'texist.

That's the job.

The Genesis Health Foundation is the philanthropic engine behind Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine — one of Chicagoland's fastest-growing, most mission-driven MSK platforms. We're 16 clinics deep, running clinical trials, serving Medicaid populations at scale, and proving every day that excellent care and accessible care are the same thing. The Foundation exists to close the last gap: ensuring that patients with no coverage, no safety net, and no other options still receive world-class orthopedic care.

We need an Executive Director to build the institution that makes that possible.

The Role

This is a founding-energy leadership position. The Foundation has the right mission, the right clinical partner, and the right story. What it needs is an operator who can turn that into a fundraising machine, a community institution, and a durable source of capital for indigent care.

You'll own everything: strategy, donor development, institutional partnerships, board management, grant operations, community presence, and the organizational infrastructure to support it all. You'll work in close partnership with the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine leadership team — with direct line of sight into the clinical impact your work is funding.

When you raise a dollar, you'll know exactly where it goes.

What You'll Drive

Major gifts and individual donor strategy: identifying, cultivating, and closing relationships with high-net-worth donors who are aligned with the mission
Institutional partnerships: foundations, health systems, corporate sponsors, and civic organizations across Chicago and beyond
Grant development and management: building and maintaining a diversified portfolio of public and private grant funding
Board development: recruiting, activating, and stewarding a board that opens doors and brings resources
Indigent care fund: designing and managing the financial mechanism that gets uninsured patients the care they need, with zero friction
Brand and storytelling: turning Genesis's clinical track record into compelling narratives that move donors to act
Organizational infrastructure — building the team, systems, and processes to operate a high-performance nonprofit

Who We're Looking For

You've done this before. You know how to build a donor pipeline, close a major gift, and manage a board that's genuinely useful. But beyond the craft of fundraising, you're motivated by something specific: the belief that access to care is a solvable problem, and that the solution requires both excellent clinical infrastructure and the financial architecture to back it up.

You're a builder, not a caretaker. You want to create something, not maintain something.

You understand both worlds. You can sit across from a major donor at a fundraising dinner and walk a clinic floor the next morning — and you know why both matter.

You lead with the mission, close with the data. Genesis has outcomes. It has patient stories. It has a model that works. You know how to translate all of that into a case for investment that sophisticated donors find compelling and irresistible.

You're Chicago-rooted or Chicago-ready. This city's philanthropic and civic ecosystem is the playing field. Knowing it — or being hungry to learn it — is essential.

The Opportunity

Competitive nonprofit executive compensation
Direct partnership with the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine leadership team
Real, measurable clinical impact — every dollar funds care for a specific patient population
Ground-floor opportunity to build a foundation with significant long-term potential
The infrastructure and credibility of an established, growing clinical operation behind you

About Genesis Health Foundation

Genesis Health Foundation is the nonprofit arm of the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine ecosystem — a full-spectrum MSK platform operating across 16 clinics in Chicagoland, conducting clinical trials, and delivering orthopedic care to Medicaid populations at scale. Our clinical model has already proven that accessible care and exceptional care aren't in conflict. The Foundation exists to extend that proof to the patients who fall outside every existing coverage structure.

We're not a charity attached to a healthcare brand. We're the financial infrastructure for a movement.

If you've spent your career building institutions that make care more equitable — and you're ready to do it at the intersection of a world-class clinical operation and the communities that need it most — we want to hear from you.

Genesis Health Foundation is actively reviewing applications.

Job Description

For forty years Lexington Habitat for Humanity, now Habitat for Humanity of Fayette and Franklin Counties, has built and repaired homes in Lexington, serving more than 500 households through homeownership, critical home repair, a ReStore and neighborhood programs. Recent production has averaged seven to nine new homes and ten to twelve critical home repairs a year. The Board is seeking a Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
to scale the organization from a charity that builds and repairs homes into an affordable housing developer with a charitable mission.

Committed initiatives are already underway. Approximately eighteen lots are coming to the organization at no land cost through the Marquard Field development. The organization is seeking Community Housing Development Organization (CHDO) designation, which could open a federal funding stream currently unavailable to it.

In September 2026, the organization announced its expansion into Franklin County and adopted the name Habitat for Humanity of Fayette and Franklin Counties. Franklin County carries the fourth-largest housing supply gap in Kentucky, a shortage of 4,457 units, with 37 percent of renters cost-burdened. Fayette County’s shortage exceeds 22,000 units. The expansion was announced alongside the Mayor of Frankfort and the Franklin County Deputy Judge-Executive, and increases access to land and funding sources. Program delivery is phasing in.

Habitat Fayette and Franklin Counties is simultaneously a social service agency, a residential construction operation, a mortgage originator and servicer, a retailer, and an affordable housing developer. Forty-seven staff. Seven department leaders report to the chief executive officer, most with more than a decade of tenure.

Specific experience managing every one of those operations is not expected. The board is looking for an executive who can lead an organization more complex than any single background prepares a person for: someone who sets direction with the team, sequences it into executable steps, holds the organization accountable for those steps and delivers.

The organization does not currently employ a Finance Director or CFO. A controller manages the books, and the Board treasurer, a CPA, is closely engaged. The organization intends to add a senior finance leader. Sequencing relative to this appointment is under discussion, and the incoming chief executive officer will be part of that decision and will carry more of the financial load until the hire is made.

Candid about where this sits. The organization has run an operating deficit for three consecutive years. For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, it held roughly $9 million in assets against $3.4 million of revenue, and the goal is a balanced budget in fiscal 2028. The Board discusses the financial position in full early in the process.

Staff retention is a defining strength. Department leaders average more than a decade with the organization, and the average ReStore associate has been in place about five years.

Responsibilities

In the first twenty-four months

Stabilize the financial position and remove going-concern language from the audit, including a sustainable operating model and a senior finance hire
Meet the organization’s commitments on Marquard Field
Increase annual home production to ten, advance CHDO designation, and secure the land pipeline

Qualifications

Financial acumen sufficient to lead a sizable and diverse organization with multiple lines of business
A demonstrated record of taking initiatives that are underway and carrying them through to completion, with the project management discipline to keep them moving
Experience working with local, state and federal partners to secure and manage capital and grant funds, together with fundraising and donor cultivation experience
Creative and innovative thinking about sustainability in affordable housing or an adjacent field
Experience leading and collaborating with an established team of subject matter experts, including change management with long-tenured staff
Clear, consistent, respectful communication with staff, board, funders and the broader community, including public advocacy for affordable housing

Preferred, Not Required

The Board reviewed the conventional screens for this role and removed the ones that would exclude strong candidates without improving the hire.

Habitat for Humanity experience
A nonprofit career. The board will evaluate for-profit and nonprofit backgrounds against the same criteria, and is actively interested in operators from outside the sector
Construction expertise. Working literacy is sufficient. The organization employs the technical experts
Knowledge of affordable housing, real estate development, or community-based housing programs
Candidates meeting most of these criteria, with genuine strength in several that matter to this organization, are encouraged to apply

Compensation

Annual Compensation: $160,000 - $180,000, plus benefits

How to Apply

Submit your resume here: https://www.lexhabitat.org/employment.

A letter of interest is welcome but not required. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as received. Open until filled.

Candidates currently in seat who would prefer a conversation before submitting an application may contact Clint Morris at [email protected] or (859) 252-2224 ext. 106.

Inquiries are held in confidence.

jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Healthcare Revenue Recovery
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Reclaim, an AI-native denial management and revenue recovery venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

We are entering a $16B+ Total Addressable Market with a gaping $ 7.5B–$10B whitespace, targeting the highly underserved mid-market segment. Currently, 30–40% of denied medical claims go uncontested because practices lack the staff and capital to contest them. This systemic failure leaves between $50,000 and $300,000 in legally earned revenue permanently abandoned at each practice every year.

Reclaim AI resolves denied and aged claims end-to-end, embedding outcome-based contingency pricing—meaning practices pay zero upfront, and we only take a cut of the dollars we successfully recover, for our target ideal customer profile (practices with $80K+ in annual recoverable claims).

Market Context

We didn’t just read market reports; we spent weeks interviewing billing managers, practice owners, revenue cycle leaders at health systems, and even digital operations leaders at major insurance companies. The dysfunction we uncovered is staggering, creating a massive opportunity for a disruptor:

The pain is so severe, practices are building their own tech: The frustration of payer opacity is so deep that medical billers are hiring part-time software engineers to build in-house robotic process automation (RPA) scrapers just to check claim statuses.
Massive, emotional write-offs: Staff carry immense guilt over these administrative losses. One small-practice assistant admitted, "I feel like we probably had to write off probably close to a million dollars" simply because they couldn't keep up with the manual follow-ups.
The "Payer-Side Inversion" Opportunity: We discovered that insurance companies are drowning in the exact same claims dysfunction they generate. One major payer we interviewed reported a backlog of 31,000 contested claims that consumed 80% of their staff's operational capacity, forcing emergency hires just to manage the disputes.
The Competition is Distracted: Well-funded Tier-1 competitors are charging $15K+ upfront licensing fees and fighting over enterprise health systems. The competitive window to capture the mid-market with a contingency-priced autonomous agent is wide open.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across vertical AI and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with practice owners and revenue cycle leaders, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

Domain & Workflow Depth: You have direct exposure to healthcare revenue cycle, medical billing, or denial management. You understand the nuanced differences in denial codes, know why administrative denials (like credentialing gaps) are uniquely painful, and intuitively understand the fragmented systems (e.g., Tebra, eClinicalWorks, Availity) that billers are forced to use

jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Retail Planning Autopilot
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Maestro, an AI-native inventory-planning intelligence venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Maestro is an autopilot planning intelligence for SMB operators managing physical inventory complexity without a planning team. It connects across channels and ERPs, handles routine decisions silently, and surfaces exceptions with context and a recommended action before they become revenue losses. The institutional memory that today lives only in a planner's head gets externalized, structured, and queried in plain language.

We didn't just build a thesis; we validated it directly with the market. We have spoken with founders, VP E-Commerce leaders, merchandise planners, and multi-channel operators at DTC and specialty retail brands across the US. The market signal is clear:

Autopilot is the vision: Every named competitor generates recommendations that humans still have to act on manually. No product at this revenue tier is building toward full autonomous execution of the planning lifecycle. Maestro's product vision is full autopilot: the system owns the buy decision, allocation, and markdown trigger end-to-end. But buyers earn that trust incrementally, starting with routine decisions handled silently and exceptions surfaced with context.
The pain is in the dollars, not the dashboards: Documented annual losses across just five buyer accounts total $1.25–1.5M+. Buyers currently spend $0–500/month on software; the entire planning budget is tied up in headcount. The payback case is immediate, and ROI demonstration, not feature demos, will be the critical sales motion.
Institutional memory failure is systemic and unresolved: One SVP with 30 years of domain expertise described relying entirely on personal recall to flag which materials, colours, and styles underperformed last season. When he leaves, that knowledge disappears, and no tool captures it today. Every buyer interviewed described a version of this problem.

Market Context

We are targeting a large, structurally underserved segment: SMB operators managing multi-channel physical inventory complexity at $5M–50M revenue — importers, distributors, Amazon aggregators, and specialty retailers. The beachhead SAM is estimated at $200M–$225M across approximately 15K–16K brands in the US and Canada. Excel is the universal incumbent! 5/5 buyers in our discovery sprint were on spreadsheets, with zero dedicated planning tools in use. The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Foundry, an AI-Native Recruiting Agency currently in build at FutureSight. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Recruiting has run on the same model for decades: firms charge a fixed percentage of a hire's first-year salary for work that is largely manual, sourcing, screening, and outreach done one candidate at a time. jobs.title: Director of Development Communications
jobs.description:
About the Role:

The Director of Development Communications leads the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of development communications for Mercatus Center. This role translates Mercatus research, policy work, organizational priorities, and impact into compelling communications that support fundraising, donor engagement, stewardship, and major-gift activity.
The Director partners closely with development leadership, major gift officers, executive leadership, subject-matter experts, marketing and design to ensure donors receive timely, relevant, and high-quality communications tailored to their interests and priorities.

This position reports to the Vice President of Development.

Specific Duties:

Lead Development Communications Strategy

Creates and implements an overarching development communications strategy aligned with fundraising goals and organizational priorities.
Establishes and communicates priorities, timelines, workflows, and project plans across development communications.
Coordinates with development leadership and cross-functional partners to ensure communications meet or exceed the team’s needs.
Assesses and secures the talent, tools, processes, and other resources necessary for the success of development communications.
Maintains high standards for accuracy, clarity, consistency, quality, and timeliness.

Develop Donor Focused Messaging

Hosts regular messaging meetings with Mercatus experts and executive leadership to identify current projects, activities, accomplishments, and outcomes relevant to donors.
Translates complex policy, research, and organizational information into clear, persuasive, and donor-centered messaging.
Develops state-specific and interest-specific communications tailored to individual donors and donor audiences.
Coordinates with state engagement, outreach, marketing, and other internal teams to incorporate relevant updates and insights.
Provides regular reports, updates, and ready-to-use messaging that help Mercatus major gift officers communicate Mercatus’ value, outputs, and outcomes.

Create Development Communications Products

Develops and maintains a broad range of high-quality fundraising, stewardship, and donor communications, including:
Prints newsletters, typically three to four times per year.
Mid-year updates, letters, and end-of-year reports.
Annual appeal prospectuses and digital annual appeals.
Regular reports for high-value donors and priority initiatives.
Ready-to-send emails highlighting policy wins, media coverage, research, events, and other organizational updates.
Media and research highlight PDFs and related donor-facing materials.
Fundraising proposals for Mercatus major donors.
Digital communications, including email newsletters, special announcements, webinar invitations, and event invitations.
Evergreen materials, such as brochures and booklets.
Additional collateral to support donor engagement, including postcards, leave-behinds, magazine or book excerpts, and other materials.

Provide Copywriting and Editorial Support

Writes and edits development emails, direct mail, lift notes, thank-you notes, proposals, reports, and other donor communications.
Provides copywriting and copy-editing support for major gift officers, development operations, and other development colleagues.
Ensures that original development communications products receive a thorough editorial review by someone other than the author before distribution.
Establishes and maintains editorial standards for development communications.

Strengthen Visual Branding

Formats documents and develop or coordinate maps, charts, graphics, and other visual elements for donor audiences.
Partners with marketing and design colleagues to ensure that development communications are consistent, polished, visually appealing, and aligned with the Mercatus brand.
Works with marketing and design teams to build and maintain a repository of high-resolution images for development use.
Helps identify opportunities to capture high-quality photography at important events and activities, including through freelance photographers when appropriate.
Develops new visual collateral and branded products to support fundraising and donor engagement.

Required Qualifications
:
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and work experience.
5 or more years of professional experience in marketing, communications, fundraising, development communications, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing communications strategies.
Exceptional writing, editing, proofreading, and storytelling skills.
Experience translating complex ideas or technical subject matter into clear, compelling communications for varied audiences.
Experience creating communications for donors, funders, executives, or other high-priority stakeholders.
Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders.
Excellent interpersonal, collaboration, and relationship-building skills.
Strong judgment, attention to detail, initiative, and follow-through.
Ability to work effectively with senior leaders, subject-matter experts, fundraisers, designers, and cross-functional teams.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
Experience with Salesforce, Canva, and email marketing platforms is a plus.
Familiarity with policy, research, nonprofit, philanthropic, or mission-driven organizations is preferred.

Success in This Role

Success in this role means that Mercatus’ development team has the strategy, messaging, content, tools, and communications support needed to engage donors effectively. The successful candidate will consistently deliver high-quality, timely, and relevant communications that clearly convey Mercatus’ mission, work, and impact while strengthening fundraising and donor relationships.

How to Apply

Please submit your cover letter and resume. Your cover letter should indicate your interest in the Mercatus Center's mission.

About the Mercatus Center

The Mercatus Center at George Mason University is where top classical liberal scholars solve real-world challenges. Grounded in the tradition of market-oriented thinking and classical liberal ideas, we equip high-agency talent to apply bold ideas that shape institutions, inform policy, and help people flourish.

Employee Benefits Review

Salary is competitive and will be commensurate with experience. In addition, Mercatus provides excellent benefits to all individual employees, including full health and dental coverage, unlimited paid time off, long-term disability and life insurance, a 403(b) retirement savings program, parking/travel benefits, and twelve free credits per year at George Mason University.

EEO Statement

The Mercatus Center is an equal employment opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

E-Verify

The Mercatus Center participates in E-Verify. Upon hire, Mercatus will provide the U.S. Social Security Administration and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security, with information from each new employee’s Form I-9 to confirm work authorization.

jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI WealthTech
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Weli, a B2B WealthTech venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Weli is an AI-native operations platform purpose-built for wealth management firms. It plugs directly into the CRM, portfolio management, and custodian systems firms already run, and executes the back-office work behind every account, account opening, money transfer, trade coordination, and compliance routing. Every wealth management firm already staffs an Operations function to do this work, typically at a ratio of roughly one Operations person to every three advisors, and that function is chronically stretched: slow, error-prone, and unable to give any single advisor's book the full attention it deserves. Weli is built for the firm's back office.

Market Context

Weli's customers are independent and hybrid RIAs, firms built around senior advisors who own their own client books and lean on a small, shared operations team to execute everything behind the scenes. It's a large and fast-growing world. There are roughly 300,000 wealth and financial advisors in the US, and the independent channel has been on a two-decade climb, from under a fifth of the industry's assets in 2007 to 27% today, on track for nearly a third by 2028.

Growth is outpacing the operations layer built to support it. The industry's leading benchmarking study found 78% of RIA firms were actively hiring last year just to keep up with capacity constraints, and most firms add a full new hire for every $360,000 of revenue growth, an expensive, linear way to scale a business that should compound. In our own interviews, one managing partner put a number on it directly: his firm could roughly triple its assets under management with its current advisor headcount if operations could keep pace. That gap, real, quantifiable, and largely unaddressed by today's AI tools, is Weli's opportunity.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across fintech and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with RIA and wealth management firms, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead a cohesive founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct exposure to wealth management, RIA operations, and financial services compliance, with the credibility and relationships to navigate the industry's regulatory landscape and sell into established firms

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Retail Planning Autopilot
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Maestro, an AI-native inventory-planning intelligence venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Maestro is an autopilot planning intelligence for SMB operators managing physical inventory complexity without a planning team. It connects across channels and ERPs, handles routine decisions silently, and surfaces exceptions with context and a recommended action before they become revenue losses. The institutional memory that today lives only in a planner's head gets externalized, structured, and queried in plain language.

We didn't just build a thesis; we validated it directly with the market. We have spoken with founders, VP E-Commerce leaders, merchandise planners, and multi-channel operators at DTC and specialty retail brands across the US. The market signal is clear:

Autopilot is the vision: Every named competitor generates recommendations that humans still have to act on manually. No product at this revenue tier is building toward full autonomous execution of the planning lifecycle. Maestro's product vision is full autopilot: the system owns the buy decision, allocation, and markdown trigger end-to-end. But buyers earn that trust incrementally, starting with routine decisions handled silently and exceptions surfaced with context.
The pain is in the dollars, not the dashboards: Documented annual losses across just five buyer accounts total $1.25–1.5M+. Buyers currently spend $0–500/month on software; the entire planning budget is tied up in headcount. The payback case is immediate, and ROI demonstration, not feature demos, will be the critical sales motion.
Institutional memory failure is systemic and unresolved: One SVP with 30 years of domain expertise described relying entirely on personal recall to flag which materials, colours, and styles underperformed last season. When he leaves, that knowledge disappears, and no tool captures it today. Every buyer interviewed described a version of this problem.

Market Context

We are targeting a large, structurally underserved segment: SMB operators managing multi-channel physical inventory complexity at $5M–50M revenue — importers, distributors, Amazon aggregators, and specialty retailers. The beachhead SAM is estimated at $200M–$225M across approximately 15K–16K brands in the US and Canada. Excel is the universal incumbent! 5/5 buyers in our discovery sprint were on spreadsheets, with zero dedicated planning tools in use. EBITDA across the $10–50M DTC cohort is compressed to 7.25% in 2025 with revenue declining ~4.6% YoY. Planning waste attacks the margin stack directly.

Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning

jobs.description:
OUR CORE VALUES: THE CCG SPIRIT

SERVICE – Lead with a servant’s heart

PROFESSIONALISM – Perform our best every day

INTEGRITY – Do what is right

RESPECT – Treat each other the way we wish to be treated

INCLUSION – Value individual differences

TEAMWORK – Communicate and collaborate to achieve our goals

Summary Of Position

Founded in 1901, ChildCareGroup’s (CCG) mission is to drive generational change by advancing early learning, family stability and workforce opportunity.

The Director of Marketing and Communications serves as ChildCareGroup’s senior marketing and communications leader, responsible for leading integrated strategies across brand, public relations, digital engagement, storytelling, and internal communications. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, this role partners closely with senior leadership to align communications with ChildCareGroup’s mission, Strategic Plan, organizational priorities, fundraising goals, reputation, and culture.

The Director leads the Marketing and Communications team, establishes department priorities and workflows, oversees messaging and brand standards, and ensures communications are clear, consistent, audience-centered, and aligned across programs, departments, and stakeholders. This role is accountable for strengthening organizational visibility, supporting executive and internal communications, guiding high-visibility and sensitive messaging, and positioning communications as a strategic asset across the organization.

Responsibilities And Essential Job Functions

Develop, implement, and continuously refine a comprehensive marketing and communications strategy aligned with ChildCareGroup’s Strategic Plan, mission, and long-term direction.
Partner closely with the Chief of Staff, CEO/President, and senior leadership as a strategic communications advisor, aligning marketing and communications priorities with executive decision-making, strategic plan implementation, leadership communications, board-related messaging, brand positioning, visibility, and reputation management.
Serve as the organization-wide lead for marketing and communications alignment, partnering with senior leaders and department heads to anticipate needs, clarify priorities, manage competing requests, and ensure consistent messaging across functions and audiences.
Lead, supervise, and develop the Marketing and Communications team by setting clear priorities, aligning work to organizational goals, supporting professional growth, managing performance, and ensuring timely, high-quality execution across communications, marketing, digital engagement, public relations, and event-related communications.
Provide strategic judgment and senior-level review for high-visibility, sensitive, crisis, change, media, and executive communications to protect organizational trust and ensure alignment with ChildCareGroup’s mission, values, priorities, and voice.
Establish department-wide planning systems, editorial calendars, project intake processes, production timelines, and approval workflows to prioritize work and ensure coordinated, high-quality execution.
Unify and tailor messaging for key audiences to clearly communicate ChildCareGroup’s two-generation approach, statewide reach, systems-level impact, and strategic priorities.
Oversee the strategy, quality, and consistency of collateral, campaigns, presentations, leadership materials, and communications assets to ensure alignment with brand standards, audience needs, and organizational priorities.
Lead the organization’s storytelling strategy by establishing priorities, standards, and systems for collecting, approving, and using narratives, visuals, and data that communicate ChildCareGroup’s mission, impact, and systems-level work.
Define department-level goals, metrics, and reporting rhythms to evaluate effectiveness, guide strategy, and improve reach, engagement, visibility, and organizational impact.
Lead internal communications strategy in partnership with the Chief of Staff, People and Culture, and senior leadership to promote transparency, reinforce culture, support employee engagement, and strengthen connection across locations and departments.
Partner strategically with Development to align fundraising communications, donor engagement, stewardship efforts, campaign messaging, and special event communications with organizational priorities and revenue goals.
Manage external marketing, communications, creative, media, and public relations partners and support related budget planning to ensure vendor work, paid campaigns, tools, and materials align with strategic priorities and brand standards.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; degree in marketing, communications, public relations, journalism, or a related field preferred.
Seven to ten years of progressive experience in marketing and communications, including experience managing staff.
Demonstrated success developing and executing integrated marketing and communications strategies.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with experience in media relations, executive-level communications, and high-visibility or sensitive messaging.
Strong project management, organizational, and analytical skills.
Experience with digital platforms, email marketing systems, social media strategy, website management, and analytics.
Nonprofit experience and familiarity with fundraising communications preferred.

Equipment

Computer, telephone headset, fax, scanner, and general office equipment.

Travel and Compliance

Valid Texas driver's license required.
Driving record must comply with CCG's automobile insurance carrier requirements.
Must have and maintain liability insurance coverage and reliable personal transportation.

Must submit to and successfully pass all required CCG and Partner Program background checks throughout employment. Background check requirements may be expanded at the discretion of CCG and Partner Programs.

Visual attention.
Manual dexterity/coordination.

jobs.description:
Overview

The Worker Empowerment Cabinet advances the well-being of Boston workers in the public and private sectors. Our goals include: (1) setting the City’s future policy and vision for workers, (2) regulating, overseeing, and improving workplace conditions and health for workers, and (3) expanding economic opportunities for workers through quality jobs, skills training, and career pipelines.

Under the direction of the Chief of Worker Empowerment, the Assistant Policy Director will play a key role in advancing workforce development and worker protection initiatives. This role involves aligning policy priorities with funding opportunities, developing and securing resources for new and existing programs, and supporting grant proposal preparation and implementation. The Assistant Policy Director will collaborate with various departments and stakeholders to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of current programs, ensure compliance with funding requirements, and identify opportunities for policy improvements. Additionally, the role includes monitoring policy issues affecting Boston residents and providing actionable recommendations to enhance workforce development strategies and workers’ protection, health, and safety.

Responsibilities

Program Development:

Collaborate with staff to align policy priorities for the Worker Empowerment Cabinet, including but not limited to workforce development, labor, alternative education, worker protections, youth employment, and economic development.
Assist in designing, developing, and implementing programs that support policy priorities and achieve measurable results in the Cabinet’s goal of providing access to good quality jobs for all Boston residents.
Align projects and programs with funding opportunities and develop sustainable funding plans for new and existing programs.
Coordinate with stakeholders, including government agencies, advocacy groups, and community organizations, to develop implementation partnerships and ensure alignment on funding proposals.

Program And Grant Oversight

Support monitoring and evaluation of programs and initiatives to assess their effectiveness.
Support the management of grant-funded projects by ensuring compliance with reporting and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate program planning for current funding sources, using research to inform the design of upcoming RFPs.
Perform research to improve the quality of oversight and technical assistance provided to grantees.
Work with various departments to ensure compliance with all funding source reporting requirements.
Collaborate with city, state, and local community partners to identify policy and program directions aligned with Cabinet objectives. Grant Management and Oversight:

Stakeholder Engagement And Advocacy

Establish and cultivate effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including government agencies, advocacy groups, community organizations, and key influencers, to ensure alignment on policy objectives, support workforce development initiatives, and identify implementation challenges and ecosystem gaps and needs.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Reclaim, an AI-native denial management and revenue recovery venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

We are entering a $16B+ Total Addressable Market with a gaping $ 7.5B–$10B whitespace, targeting the highly underserved mid-market segment. Currently, 30–40% of denied medical claims go uncontested because practices lack the staff and capital to contest them. This systemic failure leaves between $50,000 and $300,000 in legally earned revenue permanently abandoned at each practice every year.

Reclaim AI resolves denied and aged claims end-to-end, embedding outcome-based contingency pricing—meaning practices pay zero upfront, and we only take a cut of the dollars we successfully recover, for our target ideal customer profile (practices with $80K+ in annual recoverable claims).

new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Executive Director is the chief executive of Faith Community Health Network and is responsible for leading the organization, directing its operations, developing its people, managing its resources, and advancing its mission of removing barriers to healthcare for individuals who would otherwise go without it. Reporting to and partnering with the Board of Directors, the Executive Director translates the Board's strategic vision into responsible, mission-centered action across the Network and its operating entities, Faith Community Pharmacy and Faith Community Clinic.

The role carries broad decision-making authority, but its success depends on trust, communication, and coalition-building. The Executive Director serves as the organization's chief steward, protecting its mission, financial resources, reputation, relationships, and the trust of the patients, employees, volunteers, donors, partners, and Board members who make its work possible.

The Executive Director directly supervises the Director of Administration, Pharmacy Director, Clinic Director, and Program Director. Day-to-day operational execution is led by the Director of Administration, allowing the Executive Director to focus on strategy, fundraising, Board relations, major-donor relationships, and community engagement. This partnership allows the Executive Director to focus on vision, strategy, external partnerships, Board relations, major-donor relationships, and community engagement while ensuring operational excellence across the organization.

About the Organization

Faith Community Health Network is a faith-based, nonprofit charitable healthcare organization serving uninsured and underinsured individuals in Northern Kentucky. Founded on the belief that no one should have to choose between their health and their financial stability, the Network operates as the parent organization for multiple charitable healthcare ministries:

•    Faith Community Pharmacy —
a charitable pharmacy founded in 2002 that provides medications at no cost to uninsured and underinsured patients and is among the region's most established charitable pharmacy programs.
•    Faith Community Clinic —
a free clinic providing primary healthcare, chronic disease management, preventive care, and care coordination to uninsured adults, staffed by volunteer health professionals.
The Network provides centralized leadership, finance, development, human resources, strategic planning, marketing, compliance, and administrative support, allowing each operating entity to focus on delivering exceptional patient care while benefiting from shared resources and coordinated leadership. The organization works within a broad network of healthcare, academic, governmental, philanthropic, and faith community partners.

Key Responsibilities

Mission and Strategy

•   Translate the Board's strategic vision into practical, actionable plans and ensure consistent progress toward strategic objectives.
•   While understanding the organization cannot solve all unmet needs, provides continual evaluation of unmet healthcare needs in the community and assesses whether the organization is positioned to address them responsibly.
Board Partnership and Governance

•   Partner with and remain accountable to the Board of Directors, providing timely, sufficient information for thoughtful analysis, discussion, and decision-making.
•   Maintain a proactive, communicative relationship with the Board Chair, including regular written updates and early identification of significant issues.
Support the Board's ability to maintain communication channels with staff.
•   Support effective governance, committee structure, and Board engagement; implement Board policies and recommend policies for Board consideration.
•  Consult the bylaws and governance policies to determine which decisions require Board approval.
•  The Executive Committee of the Board of Directors will conduct a formal performance review of the Executive Director annually, evaluating progress against mutually established goals, financial stewardship, and organizational health.
Staff Leadership and Human Resources

•   Build, develop, and support a capable leadership team; hire strong people, give directors meaningful ownership of their areas, and hold them accountable for outcomes while cultivating autonomy.
•   Foster a positive, professional, and healthy work environment grounded in dignity, care, and respect, in which employees feel safe raising concerns and expressing differing views.
•   Provide coaching and mentoring, lead and prioritize the weekly leadership meeting, and maintain a visible, accessible presence across the Pharmacy and Clinic.
•   Ensure effective recruitment, training, retention, and personnel practices, and address workplace concerns early, honestly, and respectfully.
Fundraising and Resource Development

•   Serve as a lead relationship-builder with major donors, foundations, corporations, and government partners, communicating the organization's vision and impact.
•   Participate in major gift cultivation and solicitation, support grant development and reporting, and engage the Board in resource development.
•   Protect donor trust through timely, meaningful stewardship and by ensuring commitments are fulfilled.
•   Partner with the Director of Administration, who assists with development operations, grant management, and donor stewardship.
Financial Stewardship

•   Hold ultimate accountability for the financial health of the organization, including development of the annual budget and ongoing monitoring of revenue, expenses, and cash flow.
•   Ensure appropriate internal controls, proper use of restricted funds, and compliance with grant and contract obligations across multiple legal entities.
•   Support the audit and IRS Form 990 processes and communicate financial realities honestly to the Board.
Organizational Oversight

•   Provide overall leadership and accountability for the Network and its entities, ensuring strong operational execution through the Director of Administration and the broader leadership team.
•   Ensure high-quality, patient-centered care and build strong foundations — leadership, staffing, funding, facilities, and partnerships — before launching or expanding initiatives.
•   Ensure regulatory readiness and compliance, including initiatives such as FTCA deeming and other quality and safety standards.
Community, External Relations, and Communications

•   Serve as the organization's chief spokesperson, representing Faith Community Health Network to partners, funders, elected officials, healthcare leaders, academic institutions, and the community.
•   Develop and maintain positive relationships with community partners, donors, and key stakeholders, acting at the organizational level while thinking at the system level.
•   Strengthen the organization's reputation and visibility and pursue partnerships that expand impact without unnecessarily duplicating services.

Leadership Qualities and Competencies

The Executive Director must be capable of serving as a vision setter, coach, servant leader, chief executive, consensus builder, advocate, fundraiser, and problem solver. The following qualities are central to success in the role:
•    Confident humility —
knows what they do well and leads decisively, while remaining honest about what they do not know, listening to others, and changing course when the evidence warrants.
•    Patient-centered values —
treats every person with dignity and respect and keeps patients at the center of every decision.
•    Sound judgment —
builds consensus where possible, makes decisions when necessary, and takes responsibility for outcomes.
•    Effective communication —
communicates the vision repeatedly and clearly, recognizing that alignment must be continually renewed across staff, Board, donors, and partners.

Qualifications

Required

•   Bachelor's degree, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience.
•   Progressively responsible senior leadership experience, ideally including nonprofit or mission-driven organizations.
•   Demonstrated success in fundraising and donor relationships, financial management, and staff leadership.
•   Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors and an understanding of nonprofit governance.
•   Strong financial literacy, including budgeting, financial oversight, and internal controls.
•   Excellent communication, relationship-building, and public representation skills.
•  A commitment to the organization's mission and to serving uninsured and underinsured individuals with compassion and respect.
•   Established relationships within their community. 
Preferred

•   Advanced degree in nonprofit management, public health, healthcare administration, business, or a related field.
•   Experience in charitable healthcare, free or charitable clinics or pharmacies, or safety-net healthcare settings.
•   Grant writing and grant management experience, and familiarity with healthcare regulatory and compliance requirements.
•  Northern Kentucky / Greater Cincinnati community presence.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This is a full-time, on-site position based in Northern Kentucky. The Executive Director maintains a regular presence across the Pharmacy and Clinic and represents the organization at community, donor, and partner events, which may occasionally occur outside of standard business hours. The role involves typical office activities and the ability to move throughout the organization's facilities. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

To Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume, a cover letter describing their interest in the mission and relevant leadership experience, and three professional references to Chrissy Schreiner-Spille at: Chrissy@fchealthnetwork.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

new_jobs.title: Genesis Health Foundation - Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
The best healthcare model in the world still has a hole in it. Medicaid covers a lot. It doesn't cover everyone. There's a population that falls through every gap — uninsured, underinsured, invisible to the system — that still walks through our doors with a torn ACL, a shattered wrist, a spine that's been quietly failing them for years. They need care. They deserve it. And right now, the infrastructure to fully fund it doesn'texist.

That's the job.

The Genesis Health Foundation is the philanthropic engine behind Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine — one of Chicagoland's fastest-growing, most mission-driven MSK platforms. We're 16 clinics deep, running clinical trials, serving Medicaid populations at scale, and proving every day that excellent care and accessible care are the same thing. The Foundation exists to close the last gap: ensuring that patients with no coverage, no safety net, and no other options still receive world-class orthopedic care.

We need an Executive Director to build the institution that makes that possible.

The Role

This is a founding-energy leadership position. The Foundation has the right mission, the right clinical partner, and the right story. What it needs is an operator who can turn that into a fundraising machine, a community institution, and a durable source of capital for indigent care.

You'll own everything: strategy, donor development, institutional partnerships, board management, grant operations, community presence, and the organizational infrastructure to support it all. You'll work in close partnership with the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine leadership team — with direct line of sight into the clinical impact your work is funding.

When you raise a dollar, you'll know exactly where it goes.

What You'll Drive

Major gifts and individual donor strategy: identifying, cultivating, and closing relationships with high-net-worth donors who are aligned with the mission
Institutional partnerships: foundations, health systems, corporate sponsors, and civic organizations across Chicago and beyond
Grant development and management: building and maintaining a diversified portfolio of public and private grant funding
Board development: recruiting, activating, and stewarding a board that opens doors and brings resources
Indigent care fund: designing and managing the financial mechanism that gets uninsured patients the care they need, with zero friction
Brand and storytelling: turning Genesis's clinical track record into compelling narratives that move donors to act
Organizational infrastructure — building the team, systems, and processes to operate a high-performance nonprofit

Who We're Looking For

You've done this before. You know how to build a donor pipeline, close a major gift, and manage a board that's genuinely useful. But beyond the craft of fundraising, you're motivated by something specific: the belief that access to care is a solvable problem, and that the solution requires both excellent clinical infrastructure and the financial architecture to back it up.

You're a builder, not a caretaker. You want to create something, not maintain something.

You understand both worlds. You can sit across from a major donor at a fundraising dinner and walk a clinic floor the next morning — and you know why both matter.

You lead with the mission, close with the data. Genesis has outcomes. It has patient stories. It has a model that works. You know how to translate all of that into a case for investment that sophisticated donors find compelling and irresistible.

You're Chicago-rooted or Chicago-ready. This city's philanthropic and civic ecosystem is the playing field. Knowing it — or being hungry to learn it — is essential.

The Opportunity

Competitive nonprofit executive compensation
Direct partnership with the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine leadership team
Real, measurable clinical impact — every dollar funds care for a specific patient population
Ground-floor opportunity to build a foundation with significant long-term potential
The infrastructure and credibility of an established, growing clinical operation behind you

About Genesis Health Foundation

Genesis Health Foundation is the nonprofit arm of the Genesis Orthopedics & Sports Medicine ecosystem — a full-spectrum MSK platform operating across 16 clinics in Chicagoland, conducting clinical trials, and delivering orthopedic care to Medicaid populations at scale. Our clinical model has already proven that accessible care and exceptional care aren't in conflict. The Foundation exists to extend that proof to the patients who fall outside every existing coverage structure.

We're not a charity attached to a healthcare brand. We're the financial infrastructure for a movement.

If you've spent your career building institutions that make care more equitable — and you're ready to do it at the intersection of a world-class clinical operation and the communities that need it most — we want to hear from you.

Genesis Health Foundation is actively reviewing applications.

Job Description

For forty years Lexington Habitat for Humanity, now Habitat for Humanity of Fayette and Franklin Counties, has built and repaired homes in Lexington, serving more than 500 households through homeownership, critical home repair, a ReStore and neighborhood programs. Recent production has averaged seven to nine new homes and ten to twelve critical home repairs a year. The Board is seeking a Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
to scale the organization from a charity that builds and repairs homes into an affordable housing developer with a charitable mission.

Committed initiatives are already underway. Approximately eighteen lots are coming to the organization at no land cost through the Marquard Field development. The organization is seeking Community Housing Development Organization (CHDO) designation, which could open a federal funding stream currently unavailable to it.

In September 2026, the organization announced its expansion into Franklin County and adopted the name Habitat for Humanity of Fayette and Franklin Counties. Franklin County carries the fourth-largest housing supply gap in Kentucky, a shortage of 4,457 units, with 37 percent of renters cost-burdened. Fayette County’s shortage exceeds 22,000 units. The expansion was announced alongside the Mayor of Frankfort and the Franklin County Deputy Judge-Executive, and increases access to land and funding sources. Program delivery is phasing in.

Habitat Fayette and Franklin Counties is simultaneously a social service agency, a residential construction operation, a mortgage originator and servicer, a retailer, and an affordable housing developer. Forty-seven staff. Seven department leaders report to the chief executive officer, most with more than a decade of tenure.

Specific experience managing every one of those operations is not expected. The board is looking for an executive who can lead an organization more complex than any single background prepares a person for: someone who sets direction with the team, sequences it into executable steps, holds the organization accountable for those steps and delivers.

The organization does not currently employ a Finance Director or CFO. A controller manages the books, and the Board treasurer, a CPA, is closely engaged. The organization intends to add a senior finance leader. Sequencing relative to this appointment is under discussion, and the incoming chief executive officer will be part of that decision and will carry more of the financial load until the hire is made.

Candid about where this sits. The organization has run an operating deficit for three consecutive years. For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, it held roughly $9 million in assets against $3.4 million of revenue, and the goal is a balanced budget in fiscal 2028. The Board discusses the financial position in full early in the process.

Staff retention is a defining strength. Department leaders average more than a decade with the organization, and the average ReStore associate has been in place about five years.

Responsibilities

In the first twenty-four months

Stabilize the financial position and remove going-concern language from the audit, including a sustainable operating model and a senior finance hire
Meet the organization’s commitments on Marquard Field
Increase annual home production to ten, advance CHDO designation, and secure the land pipeline

Qualifications

Financial acumen sufficient to lead a sizable and diverse organization with multiple lines of business
A demonstrated record of taking initiatives that are underway and carrying them through to completion, with the project management discipline to keep them moving
Experience working with local, state and federal partners to secure and manage capital and grant funds, together with fundraising and donor cultivation experience
Creative and innovative thinking about sustainability in affordable housing or an adjacent field
Experience leading and collaborating with an established team of subject matter experts, including change management with long-tenured staff
Clear, consistent, respectful communication with staff, board, funders and the broader community, including public advocacy for affordable housing

Preferred, Not Required

The Board reviewed the conventional screens for this role and removed the ones that would exclude strong candidates without improving the hire.

Habitat for Humanity experience
A nonprofit career. The board will evaluate for-profit and nonprofit backgrounds against the same criteria, and is actively interested in operators from outside the sector
Construction expertise. Working literacy is sufficient. The organization employs the technical experts
Knowledge of affordable housing, real estate development, or community-based housing programs
Candidates meeting most of these criteria, with genuine strength in several that matter to this organization, are encouraged to apply

Compensation

Annual Compensation: $160,000 - $180,000, plus benefits

How to Apply

A letter of interest is welcome but not required. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as received. Open until filled.

Candidates currently in seat who would prefer a conversation before submitting an application may contact Clint Morris at [email protected] or (859) 252-2224 ext. 106.

Inquiries are held in confidence.
